title: Chicken a la King
subtitle: Chicken and mushrooms in a rich cream sauce
excerpt: Tender chicken breast and mushrooms in a buttery, lightly spiced cream sauce. Served over toast, rice, or pastry shells, this is classic American diner comfort food.
sourceNotes: American dish with origins in the late nineteenth century. Standard diner version uses cream sauce with peppers and pimentos.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the sauce and chicken without any pastry or rice. Thaw overnight and reheat gently, adding a splash of stock if the sauce is too thick.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Make a double batch and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Add the cooked chicken when reheating.

content.text: Chicken a la King is a creamy pan sauce with vegetables and tender chicken. It needs a good base of stock and cream rather than just cream alone. Serve it over toast or rice so nothing is wasted.
Melt half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper. Brown them in batches for 3 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining butter to the same pan. Cook the onion over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the mushrooms and peppers. Cook for 5 minutes until the mushrooms are golden and any liquid has evaporated.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables. Stir well and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the hot stock a ladleful at a time, whisking after each addition. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cream and paprika. Return the chicken to the pan. Simmer for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce coats a spoon.
Add the peas if using and cook for 2 more minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Scatter with parsley and serve over toast or rice.

items.cause: The stock was added too fast before the flour fully hydrated.
items.fix: Whisk vigorously and strain through a sieve if needed. Add remaining stock more slowly next time.

items.symptom: The chicken is rubbery and dry.
items.cause: It was overcooked or the pieces were too small.
items.fix: Cut larger pieces and simmer gently; remove the chicken as soon as it is just cooked through.

items.cause: The mushrooms released a lot of water into the sauce.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes to reduce. Make sure mushrooms are golden before adding flour.
